name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
title: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
answer: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running a language model on hardware the organisation controls, either on its own network or on a machine with no outside connection at all. In legal operations the driver is usually confidentiality: client matter files, privileged advice and deal documents that cannot be sent to a hosted API. The scope covers the model weights, the inference server that runs them, the hardware they sit on, and the surrounding controls that keep the whole stack inside the firm's boundary. It is a deployment pattern rather than a product, and it can be applied to a single workstation or to a shared cluster.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running a language model on hardware the organisation controls, either on its own network or on a machine with no outside connection at all. In legal operations the driver is usually confidentiality: client matter files, privileged advice and deal documents that cannot be sent to a hosted API. The scope covers the model weights, the inference server that runs them, the hardware they sit on, and the surrounding controls that keep the whole stack inside the firm's boundary. It is a deployment pattern rather than a product, and it can be applied to a single workstation or to a shared cluster.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The stack starts with hardware, typically one or more GPUs with enough memory to hold the model weights and the context being processed, plus ordinary server components around them. On top sits an inference runtime that loads the weights and serves requests, with common choices including llama.cpp, Ollama and vLLM. A private model registry or file store holds the weights, and an internal gateway handles authentication, logging and routing so that no request leaves the network. Air-gapped setups add physical separation: no outbound internet, controlled media transfer, and a separate update path for models and patches.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work begins with model selection, weighing parameter count and quantisation against the accuracy a legal task actually needs, since a smaller model that fits the available memory often beats a larger one that does not. The chosen weights are pulled once, verified, and stored internally, then loaded by the inference server and exposed through an internal endpoint. Evaluation comes next: a set of representative tasks, such as summarising a contract or answering questions over a document set, run against the local model and compared with the hosted baseline. Prompting, retrieval over the firm's own document store, and light fine-tuning are the usual levers for closing any quality gap.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main obligations are confidentiality, records and accountability. Because prompts and outputs stay on firm hardware, data handling is governed by internal policy and client engagement terms rather than by a vendor's terms of service, and the audit trail has to be built deliberately through logging and access control. Model provenance matters: the licence attached to the weights, the source it came from, and the version in use all need to be recorded, and open-weight licences vary in what they permit. Where a deployment touches personal data, the usual privacy analysis still applies, and any output used in advice or filing remains subject to human review and the applicable rules of professional conduct.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Two pressures are shaping this area. One is capability: open-weight models keep improving, and quantisation and serving techniques keep lowering the hardware needed to run a useful one, which widens the set of firms for which local deployment is practical. The other is oversight: as regulators and courts pay closer attention to how AI is used in legal work, an on-premises stack with its own logs and version records becomes easier to explain than a chain of external services. Expect more hybrid patterns, where sensitive material stays local and less sensitive work goes to hosted models, with the boundary between the two written down and enforced.
